title: Immune Mechanisms Regulating Allergy
text:
IgE is an antibody produced by B cells in people with food allergies and asthma, and it can cause life-threatening
anaphylaxis, especially in those with food allergy. We discovered a new type of T cell that promotes B cell
production of IgE, but we do not know how the signals from this T cell control the IgE B cell response. Our lab
developed the techniques necessary to discover these molecular pathways in human and mouse B cells that
promote anaphylaxis-inducing IgE.

title: Plant-derived nanoparticles as a sepsis therapy
text:
Sepsis is a life-threatening condition driven by uncontrolled inflammation that leads to multiple organ failure,
yet no FDA-approved therapy exists to improve survival. This project develops novel bio-inspired triglyceride-
ceramide lipid nanoparticles (TCNP) and Dexamethasone-loaded TCNP (Dex-TCNP) as a scalable, dual-
action nanotherapy that combines broad and highly effective inflammation-scavenging properties with
controlled drug delivery to restore immune balance in sepsis. If successful, this approach will establish a safe,
rapidly acting, and clinically translatable nanoparticle platform to improve outcomes in sepsis and other severe
inflammatory diseases.

title: Ultrahigh Speed, Widefield OCT Angiography System for Patients who are Unable to Cooperate
text:
Systemic and ocular diseases affecting retinal vascular development, perfusion, and neovascularization are
preventable causes of moderate to severe vision impairment in millions of people worldwide. While many adults
can cooperate with and hold still for advanced retinal imaging, a significant number of patients (including infants,
young children, and older patients who are unable to cooperate) cannot, and thus cannot access these advanced
imaging technologies that provide valuable diagnostic information and advance our understanding of disease. In
this Small Business Innovation Research proposal, we propose to develop an ultra-high-speed widefield
handheld OCTA device that will provide physicians a valuable research and diagnostic tool for imaging of these
underserved patients.

title: Primary screening and hit follow up to identify the first selective inhibitors of PLC?1 and PLC?2
text:
Dysfunction of either of the two phospholipase C gamma family members, PLCγ1 and PLCγ2 have been
implicated as driving oncogenesis through activating mutants or oncofusion protein-induced upregulation.
Utilizing a newly developed fluorescent solution-based substrate created by our lab, C8CF3-coumarin, and a
literature reported liposome-based substrate, XY-69, we will perform a high-throughput screen on both PLCγ1
and PLCγ2 to identify the first known selective inhibitors. Through the use of biochemical, biophysical, and
cellular orthogonal assays, we will validate hit scaffolds that can be further developed into useful chemical probes
or potential therapeutics upon further investment.

title: Use of Next-Gen Sequencing to Identify Genetic Variants that Influence compulsive Oxycodone Intake in Outbred Rats
text:
This is a multidisciplinary, highly collaborative consortium that combines next-generation sequencing with
state-of-the-art behavioral screening in a unique, genetically diverse, nonhuman animal model. The goals of
this consortium are to identify gene variants that are associated with oxycodone use, the effects of oxycodone
on analgesia and pain using genome-wide association studies (GWAS), and the sensitivity to FDA-approved
treatments in behaviorally characterized heterogeneous stock rats, and to maintain a data/tissue repository
(Oxycodone BioBank) accessible to all researchers to study the cellular and molecular mechanisms of
oxycodone addiction. Results from these studies have the potential to have a sustained and powerful impact
on the field of addiction because they will identify novel druggable targets, provide a comprehensive analysis of
oxycodone addiction-like behaviors in males and females, and maintain a unique data/tissue repository that will
facilitate follow-up and replication studies.

title: Novel Therapeutics to Treat HPV-Associated Cancers
text:
There is no specific medical therapy for human papillomavirus (HPV) induced cancers, which
cause ~5% of cancers worldwide. Kovina Therapeutics has developed drug-like molecules that
block the activity of a key HPV protein which is always present in HPV induced cancers. This
grant application proposes the necessary formulation development and testing to produce
sufficient quantities and quality of the prospective drug and to characterize its pharmacology
prior to initiating an in-human clinical trial.

title: Impact of prenatal opioid exposure on neurobehavioral development
text:
Prenatal opioid exposure (PODE) is related to behavioral and cognitive deficits that emerge during infancy and
persist through adolescence, but the neural mechanisms driving these divergent trajectories are virtually
unknown. This project will advance our understanding of the impact of PODE on neurobehavioral development
by investigating longitudinal trajectories of brain structure-function coupling and identifying associations between
neurocircuitry, environmental factors, and behavioral outcomes. Findings will not only inform early intervention
strategies and personalized treatments for affected infants but also contribute to promoting healthier outcomes
for this vulnerable population.

title: Core B - BWH Nanoparticle Core
text:
CORE B- Narrative
Core B will formulate nanoparticles, encapsulate the payloads, and carry out nanoparticle surface conjugation
with antibodies to be used by investigators of this program project grant. Core B will advance precision
medicine in the treatment of patients with lupus nephritis.

title: Reprogramming and Directed Differentiation of Skeletal Muscle Cells from hPSCs
text:
This proposal aims to understand and interrogate the differences in skeletal muscle progenitor cells (SMPCs)
compared to adult satellite cells (SCs) both molecularly and functionally to enable generation of more
regenerative cells from human pluripotent stem cells (hPSCs). Generation of the most regenerative SMPC or
SC-like cells from hPSCs could improve our ability to model muscle diseases in a dish and have the potential
for use in personalized cell replacement therapies.

title: Targeting ZNF410 for HbF reactivation
text:
Induction of fetal hemoglobin in adult red blood cells could serve as a functional cure for sickle cell disease and
beta-thalassemia, which are among the most common single gene disorders in the world, continue to exhibit
unmet clinical need, and affect populations impacted by health disparities. Recently a new molecular
mechanism has been discovered to silence fetal hemoglobin in adult red blood cells based on a gene called
ZNF410. This proposal explores the hypothesis that targeting ZNF410 could be a promising approach to
therapeutically induce fetal hemoglobin—by understanding how ZNF410 controls gene expression,
investigating the biological functions of ZNF410, and evaluating small molecules that degrade ZNF410.

title: Pragmatic and automated pressure injury detection across a heterogeneous patient population
text: The incidence rates of pressure injuries are on the rise, intensifying the workload for nurses. Our project aims to improve early detection of pressure injuries across all patients by implementing a validated, automated noninvasive thermography approach seamlessly integrated into the standard clinical workflow. The anticipated outcomes include the successful implementation of a nursing-informed thermography approach, contributing to a significant reduction in pressure injuries and ultimately leading to improved patient outcomes.

title: Interpretable Deep Learning Models for Analysis of Longitudinal 3D Mammography Screenings
text:
Routine mammography screening for early cancer detection has significantly reduced breast cancer mortality,
but also subjects women to several potential harms, including incorrect results and unnecessary recall with po-
tentially invasive procedures. The goal of this project is to increase accuracy of breast cancer detection and
risk estimation through the development of new deep learning models that consider a patient’s mammogram
screening history. This work would improve breast cancer detection, inform individualized screening protocols,
and guide development and monitoring of tissue-modifying preventive cancer treatments.

title: Imaging cerebral metabolic impairment in AD using Deuterium MRI
text:
The proposed research will validate new metabolic imaging approaches allowing for improved non-invasive
assessment of impaired glucose metabolism in Alzheimer’s disease (AD). Upon clinical translation, the methods
developed in this proposal will serve to ameliorate clinical management of people living with AD, help refine
therapeutic regimens and, ultimately, lead to better outcome and patient quality of life.

title: Developing technologies to identify dynamics of PTM enzyme-substrate networks during infections
text:
Post-translational modifications (PTMs) involve the covalent attachment of functional groups (chemical and
protein) to proteins following their biosynthesis. These modifications facilitate precise, rapid, and reversible
regulation of the proteome but our understanding of their functional relevance is limited due the lack of techniques
which can directly connect PTM enzymes to their substrate sites. This proposal aims to develop innovative
proteomic strategies that directly link PTM enzymes (for ubiquitylation, phosphorylation, methylation and
acetylation) to their regulators and substrate modification sites, and to determine how the networks of PTMs are
rewired by viruses to promote infection and counter host defenses.

title: National Center for Foundational Artificial Intelligence for Rehabilitation (FAIR Center)
text:
Millions of people suffer from pain and loss of independence due to conditions like osteoarthritis,
cerebral palsy, stroke, and age-related frailty, which limit their ability to move. Although vast
amounts of data have been collected by hundreds of movement research labs, these data
remain siloed in isolated labs and have been minimally utilized to understand and improve the
rehabilitation of individuals with these conditions. Our project will overcome this barrier by
curating a high-quality, large-scale dataset to characterize human movement, and developing
powerful tools that leverage artificial intelligence (AI) to revolutionize how we diagnose, monitor,
treat, and prevent conditions that impair human movement.

title: Drug Delivery and Molecular Sensing
text: Drug Delivery and Molecular Sensing (DDMS) Research Program Project Summary The Drug Delivery and Molecular Sensing (DDMS) Research Program at Purdue University develops physical science, engineering, and technology-based solutions to advance the understanding of cancer biology and improve the prevention, detection, and treatment of cancer. The program integrates expertise from the Purdue Institute for Cancer Research (PICR) Foundational Disciplines into collaborative studies, leveraging DDMS strengths in multiscale imaging modalities, tissue models for disease prognosis, molecular conjugates and nanoparticles for targeted drug delivery and surgical guidance, and therapeutic cell engineering for cancer immunotherapy. Comprising 29 faculty members from 10 academic departments, the DDMS Program fosters synergistic collaborations with other PICR Research Programs, as evidenced by a strong record of inter- programmatic publications. During the current funding period, DDMS investigators have achieved significant advances, including the development of novel nanoparticle formulations for local and systemic delivery of chemoimmunotherapy and radiotherapy, the engineering of immune cells for cancer immunotherapy, and the advancement of super-resolution optical imaging techniques for cancer cells and tissues. Additional breakthroughs include high-throughput tracking of single-molecule dynamics in CAR T cells, the creation of a mobile microrobotic system for targeted diagnostics and drug delivery, and the commercialization of a second- generation desorption electrospray ionization (DESI) XS system. Over the past five years, the program has embraced emerging research initiatives in cancer immunotherapy, radiation therapy, and cell engineering while maintaining a critical mass of expertise in biomedical imaging and therapeutic delivery technologies. Building on this foundation, the DDMS Program will continue to pursue four specific aims in the next funding period: (1) to promote excellence in drug delivery to enable advanced cancer therapies; (2) to promote excellence in molecular imaging to elucidate cancer mechanisms; (3) to integrate artificial intelligence and machine learning into imaging and diagnostics; and (4) to enhance the role of physical sciences and engineering in oncology research and innovation. These aims align with the NIH mission by supporting innovative, interdisciplinary research that addresses critical challenges in cancer toward improved health outcomes for all.

title: Generalizable quantitative imaging and machine learning signatures in glioblastoma, for precision diagnostics and personalized treatment: the ReSPOND consortium
text:
Glioblastoma (GBM) has a grim prognosis with median survival of approximately 14-16 months
which hasn't changed in over 15 years. Machine learning has offered great promise in a number of
areas in which complex information is to be synthesized for decision making. The current project
proposes to refine quantitative imaging methods leveraging machine learning (QIML), with
emphasis on a) obtaining rich imaging phenotypes relying on multi-parametric signals, textures,
shape properties, spatial patterns derived from atlas registration, and biophysical models of tumor
growth, and b) integrating such imaging signatures using machine learning into predictors of clinical
outcome, as well as of early recurrence from peri-tumoral infiltration. A unique consortium of 14
leading institutions internationally and over 4,500 patients/MRIs will be leveraged for training and
testing these QIMLs. This unique software and data resource will likely further mobilize a broad
community of quantitative imaging researchers of GB around the world and provide precision
diagnostics and personalized AI-guided treatments.

title: Deciphering piRNA-based immunity in germ cells across space and time
text:
Proper control of gene expression in germ cells is essential for fertility and for
preventing the inheritance of genetic and epigenetic errors. This research aims to
uncover how RNA-based regulatory systems and cellular condensates distinguish self
from non-self RNAs to maintain genome integrity across generations. Understanding
these mechanisms may offer insights into infertility, transgenerational diseases, and
novel RNA-based therapeutic strategies.

title: Dynamic Nanofibrous Hydrogels for Enhancing Stem Cells' Therapeutic Potency
text:
The use of hMSCs to treat diverse diseases has recently shown an exponential increase in demand;
therefore, it could become a big problem if the cell manufacturing field cannot accommodate the production line
to supply future needs. Currently, many of the static in-vitro substrates, conventional culture, and bioreactors
systems have offered a substantial benefit for generating high cell numbers, but with limited therapeutic
capabilities. This proposal aims to address that limitation by designing a dynamic composite of electrospun-
fibers encapsulated in a hydrogel that replicate the dynamic mechanics and topographical structure of native
ECM toward high hMSCs production with relevant therapeutic value.

title: Mechanisms of Serrated Colon Tumor Suppression
text:
Serrated tumors are a subset of colon tumors with especially poor prognosis, and while these
tumors are believed to initiate with mutations to the BRAF gene, the immediate consequences
of these mutations within cancer-initiating cells remain unclear. Using new technologies, the
proposed research will investigate changes in gene regulatory mechanisms in the moments
after oncogenic mutations in BRAF. The proposed studies are significant in that they will
facilitate chemoprevention, early detection, and/or tumor-suppression strategies for Serrated
colon cancer.
